title: Remove role=all entirely — split multi-process (launcher) is the ONLY mode
description: User directive (emphatic, repeated): kill role=all forever, remove it from the code; the shell must ONLY run as the split multi-process architecture (launcher supervises core + desktop + taskbar; Explorer per-window). role=all (single process, all shell windows in ONE NSApplication) is the source of the user's daily-usage problems (e.g. clicking a taskbar button raises ALL shell windows because they share one NSApp). Blast radius: 17 refs in src (RoleSelection.cs, CompositionRoot.cs, App.axaml.cs) + 5 in tests (RoleSelectorTests.cs). Remove ShellRole.All from the enum; no-args/unknown => Launcher; collapse every 'role is All or X' to X; fix default params (CompositionRoot role param, App.Role). Program.cs: default the split roles to include Desktop (Core+Desktop+Taskbar) so the desktop the user had in role=all is preserved (keep BEVEL_ENABLE_DESKTOP only as a disable override, or drop the temp gate). Update RoleSelectorTests. Update CLAUDE.md/CODEMAP (dev run 'dotnet run -- --pal=fake' now implies launcher). Full suite must stay green; real-PAL split boot validated on-device.

title: Taskbar/Start-menu MVVM redesign: background shell-model service + observable collections + off-thread cached icons (never block UI thread)
description: User-directed architecture fix. Root problem: shell does model work on the UI thread and mutates the view imperatively. Target: (1) background ShellModel service owning ObservableCollection<TaskButton> (windows) + ObservableCollection<Program> (apps) + async icon cache, all updated off the UI thread; (2) TaskbarViewModel/StartMenuViewModel thin projections; (3) view = virtualized ItemsControl + DataTemplate, no hand-rolled UpsertButton/Items.Add; (4) icons render off-thread (Task.Run) cached by (path,size), lazy per visible item; (5) enumerate apps warm at startup off-thread. Decisions: Full MVVM (not incremental); model lives in a dedicated background service (not the view-model). Also fix settings load to not block UI thread. See bd memory never-block-ui-thread.
notes:
Added requirement: taskbar button changes ANIMATED like Windows XP — buttons fade/grow in when a window opens, fade/shrink out when it closes, and width changes (as the strip fills) transition smoothly. Implement via Avalonia Transitions on the button DataTemplate (Opacity+Width) for add + resize; exit animation coordinated by ShellModel delaying the collection Remove (set IsClosing → animate → remove after ~150ms, via a non-blocking DispatcherTimer/Task.Delay+Post, never blocking the UI thread).

PENDING USER VERIFY: animations actually animate live; disappear works. NOT DONE: START MENU rewire — bind Programs to ShellModel.Programs as a virtualized ItemsControl, instant open, lazy icons (ProgramItemViewModel.EnsureIcon already written but unused; StartMenu.axaml.cs still on the old eager 284-icon path that froze ~2s). Next concrete step = rewrite StartMenu to bind + virtualize.

title: Startup deadlock: SettingsService.LoadAsync().GetResult() on UI thread hangs when settings.json exists
description: App.axaml.cs OnFrameworkInitializationCompleted blocks the Avalonia UI thread with settings.LoadAsync().GetAwaiter().GetResult(). LoadAsync awaits File.ReadAllTextAsync with default ConfigureAwait(true), so the continuation is posted back to the blocked UI SynchronizationContext -> deadlock. Only triggers when ~/.config/bevel/settings.json EXISTS (first run skips the await via File.Exists gate, so it went unnoticed in bevel-wym). Symptoms: process alive + foreground GUI app but zero windows on screen, and ignores SIGTERM (RequestExit posts Shutdown to the non-pumping dispatcher). Exposed by bevel-0ml taskbarRows persistence which guarantees the file exists. Fix: ConfigureAwait(false) on the file I/O awaits in SettingsService so it is safe to block on from the UI thread. Diagnosed via macOS 'sample': main-thread parked in Monitor_Wait/SyncBlock::Wait.
notes: FIXED + VERIFIED LIVE (uncommitted). Fix: ConfigureAwait(false) on SettingsService LoadAsync/SaveAsync/UpdateAsync file I/O + moved the startup LoadAsync().GetResult() from App.OnFrameworkInitializationCompleted to Program.Main BEFORE StartWithClassicDesktopLifetime (loads before the thread becomes the UI thread). App now shows windows + honours SIGTERM even with settings.json present. Ready to commit.
close_reason: Verified fix present in working tree: SettingsService Load/Save/UpdateAsync all use ConfigureAwait(false) on file I/O (SettingsService.cs:61,105,112,119); startup load moved to Program.Main:48 before StartWithClassicDesktopLifetime; App.axaml.cs no longer blocks the UI thread on LoadAsync. Verified live per bead notes.

title: vk4n: taking menu key focus activates the whole Bevel app, raising all shell windows (role=all)
description: Clicking a GROUPED taskbar button (opens a windows-list flyout) makes the taskbar window key via TaskbarWindow.MakeKey => makeKeyAndOrderFront: (bevel-vk4n SetKeyFocusAllowed, TaskbarWindow.cs:352). For a not-currently-active app that ACTIVATES the whole Bevel NSApplication. Third regression facet of vk4n (after the stomp, bevel-nxic). Must keep vk4n's keyboard reachability (WCAG 2.1.1) working. Milder in split mode (taskbar is its own process) but bad in the shipped role=all. Live/on-device validation required.

title: Launch/TCC hygiene: build-output apphosts pollute Spotlight; nothing opens from Apps menu + Screen Recording re-prompts every start
description:
TWO user-reported symptoms, ONE root cause. (1) Launching 'Bevel' from the Applications menu/Spotlight opens nothing. (2) Screen Recording is requested once or MORE per start.

ROOT CAUSE: every .NET build output named Bevel.App carries an embedded __TEXT,__info_plist (macOS apphost bakes one in), so Spotlight indexes each as kMDItemKind=Application. 15 'Bevel' launchables exist: 1 real dist/Bevel.app (pl.ikari.bevel, Apple-Development-signed, works) + 14 junk apphosts (bin/Debug, bin/Release, test hosts, tools/BevelShot, Bevel.IconPreview, dist/publish-app, a git worktree) that are UNSIGNED or ad-hoc and headless. Launching a junk copy => no shell window + a Screen Recording prompt that can never persist (ad-hoc/unsigned = new TCC identity each launch). 'Multiple prompts per start' also because the main app (pl.ikari.bevel) and the helper (pl.ikari.bevel.helper) are SEPARATE ScreenCapture TCC subjects. Even the real dist app is dev-signed (not Developer ID + notarized), so its grant drops on rebuild (cdhash churn, per CLAUDE.md).

lsregister -u of the junk paths is NOT durable: Spotlight re-classifies from the embedded plist and every dotnet build re-creates them.

DURABLE FIX (proposed, needs care):
- Kill pollution at source: set <UseAppHost>false</UseAppHost> for test/tool projects, and for Bevel.App except when packaging (gate on a BevelPackaging prop that build-app.sh sets). VERIFY RoleProcessSupervisor still spawns children correctly in dev (RoleProcess launches Environment.ProcessPath --role=<role>; with no apphost under 'dotnet run' ProcessPath is the dotnet muxer, so child args would need the dll — must not break multi-process dev).
- Single canonical signed install the user launches (e.g. /Applications or ~/Applications), not a deep bin path.
- For TCC persistence across rebuilds: use Developer ID + notarization (sign-app.sh path already exists) for the stable install, or accept re-grant during dev.
- Reduce to ONE Screen Recording prompt: consolidate ScreenCaptureKit into a single subject (helper-only) so app+helper don't each prompt.
- Optionally have build-app.sh/dev-sign.sh run lsregister to keep dist canonical, and add a Spotlight-exclusion (.metadata_never_index via an MSBuild target writing into OutDir) so build outputs stop being indexed.

IMMEDIATE MITIGATION done this session: unregistered the 14 junk paths from LaunchServices + re-registered dist/Bevel.app (non-durable).
notes: RESOLVED (Screen Recording): after the notarized canonical /Applications install + a clean tccutil reset, the grant STICKS across launches (user confirmed: allowed once, restart-bevel, no re-prompt). TCC.db now shows pl.ikari.bevel bundle-id = allowed (2). The risky disclaim-spawn native change was NOT needed — the per-launch re-prompt was driven by the unsigned/ad-hoc junk-copy launches + confused/stale TCC state, all fixed by the single notarized identity. Remaining nice-to-have (separate, low priority): true single prompt (app+helper are still two subjects, but each is now a one-time persistent grant); optional dist/ Spotlight exclusion.
close_reason: DONE. (1) Depollution at source (UseAppHost gating + per-OutDir .metadata_never_index) shipped earlier; (2) canonical notarized /Applications/Bevel.app install; (3) Screen Recording persistence CONFIRMED by user; (4) single Screen-Recording prompt needs NO code — with the notarized identity the helper inherits the app grant (TCC: only pl.ikari.bevel allowed, no helper row, user sees no re-prompt); (5) build-app.sh now writes .metadata_never_index into dist/ + static markers in native/ae-probe*/out so repo build output stops shadowing the canonical app in the app list (commit ee3980e). Launchpad already shows exactly one Bevel (it never lists deep ~/src paths). Residual: a few already-indexed dist/src/ae-probe entries linger in Spotlight SEARCH until a reindex — markers block re-indexing; immediate purge only via 'sudo mdutil -E /' (whole-volume rebuild), left to user discretion. Worktree checkout picks up Directory.Build.targets on its next rebuild.

title: Apple Event get/count/exists blocks the UI thread on unbounded VFS I/O
description: ce-code-review session E, maintainability P1 (validated: real never-block-UI violation; standards' 'deliberate/deadlock-safe' downgrade conflated deadlock-safety with boundedness). AppleEventBridge.cs:65 does GetAwaiter().GetResult() on AppleEventObjectResolver.ResolveAsync, which for EveryElement/ElementByName specifiers calls VfsRoot.EnumerateAsync with AllItems (IncludeHidden+System, Limit=0/unbounded); LocalFsProvider does sync Directory.EnumerateFileSystemEntries + per-entry File.GetAttributes with no cap or offload. The AE handler runs on the UI thread (Avalonia AE dispatch), so 'count of every file of folder <bigDir>' freezes the UI for the full enumeration. Fix (architectural, not mechanical): make AppleEventInbound.QueryHandler support an ASYNC reply path so Answer can await instead of GetResult(), OR isolate the enumeration off the UI thread, OR cap it. Off-thread-then-block still blocks; a cap changes count semantics — the async reply path is the real fix.
close_reason: UI-thread get/count/exists bounded via UiThreadEnumerationCap + short-circuiting ExistsAsync; async command path stays uncapped. Subteam-implemented, two adversarial verifiers SOUND, 4 tests. Native suspend/resume async reply is N/A (no such interop in repo).

title: Taskbar accessibility: keyboard reachability + screen-reader naming
description: ce-code-review session C, accessibility (headline finding). The taskbar is entirely keyboard-unreachable on macOS: TaskbarWindow SetCanBecomeKeyWindow(false) unconditionally + every control Focusable=False, so Start/task-buttons/tray/menus can't be reached or operated without a mouse (WCAG 2.1.1 failure), and the wired Ctrl+Esc/Option+Esc handler is dead code because the window never receives keystrokes. This is a DESIGN task, not a mechanical fix — needs a policy decision on the approach. Reviewer's prioritized plan: (1) give the taskbar a narrow path to key focus, e.g. become-key only while the Start menu or a task-button context menu is open (like macOS menu-bar-extra popovers); (2) flip Focusable=False→True on Start button, window ToggleButtons, folder-stack buttons, overflow chevrons + add AutomationProperties.Name bindings (window buttons→Title, tray icons→Tooltip, stacks→Name); (3) explicit .Focus() in StartMenu.OpenAsync; (4) :focus-visible style on Luna lunarow/footer button classes (WCAG 2.4.7); (5) text alt for the folder-stack 'new items' dot + AutomationProperties.Name on Onboarding sliders. Zero AutomationProperties usage anywhere in Bevel.Taskbar/Bevel.Desktop today; grouped-window and folder-stack rows are plain Borders with Tapped handlers (no automation peer, no keyboard operability).

Mechanical: Focusable+Name on Start/task/tray/stack/chevrons, Enter/Space on group+stack Border rows, :focus-visible Luna styles, stack-dot text alt, Onboarding slider names. Subteam, both verifiers SOUND, 5 tests, 801 green. Runtime prereq: from-idle hotkey needs Input Monitoring TCC grant.

title: bevel://launch: allowlist/validate the launch target (no arbitrary rooted path)

title: Single-item reveal via synthetic Cmd-drag (park one item right of the control)
description:
Click a hidden tray icon -> reveal exactly ONE real item + open its menu (user-chosen end state, bevel-7hf4). Overlay is abandoned; this rides the off-screen-push hide (MacMenuBarControl, app-side).

GEOMETRY (probed live, macOS 26, external display):
- Hidden: mirrored items at x=-5053..-3503 (OFF-screen left). BevelTrayControl at x=-3487 width~5002 -> right edge x=1515, fills visible bar 0..1515. Only items RIGHT of x=1515 stay on-screen (the Control-Center native cluster: AudioVideoModule/BentoBox/Clock).
- Un-hidden: all reflow; even then ~7 leftmost items are on=n (macOS overflow behind the app menus, x<450). Status items span x~450..1583.
- KEY: the ONLY visible slot after re-hide is RIGHT of the control's right edge (x>=1515), i.e. among the CC cluster.

MECHANISM: app orchestrates. (1) MacMenuBarControl.SetHidden(false) reveal; wait ~400ms reflow. (2) helper Cmd-drag item X from its on-screen pos to just left of the CC cluster / right of the control (~x=1515) via synthetic maskCommand mouse down+dragged+up. (3) MacMenuBarControl.SetHidden(true) re-hide; X parked right-of-control stays visible. (4) AX-press X -> menu opens at top. (5) restore: drag X back / rehide on menu-dismiss or timeout.

BUILD: new helper RPC (cmd-drag relocate) — proto change + regen (Swift+C#); extend forwardClick path (clickViaCGEvent already shows the CGEvent synth pattern to base the drag on); app orchestration in MacOSSystemTrayHost.ForwardClickAsync; MacMenuBarControl already has SetHidden.

GATING RISK (validate FIRST): does a SYNTHETIC Cmd-drag actually move Control-Center-hosted items on macOS 26? Real user Cmd-drag works; synthetic is unproven. Minimal test: drag one on-screen item by a delta, re-dump geometry, confirm it moved. If synthetic drag doesn't move CC items, this approach is dead and we fall back to reveal-neighbors or menu-only.

Fragility: drag coordinates, reflow timing, park-slot exactness (must land right of x=1515), and restoring order. Needs live iteration (user clicks; observe via the /tmp/bevel-geo probe already wired in enumerateWithCapture, gated by /tmp/bevel-geo dir).

comments.author: ikari
comments.text: ICE MECHANISM (studied jordanbaird/Ice MenuBarItemManager.swift, ~/Downloads/Ice.zip). Our cursor-warp + .cghidEventTap approach is RD-blocked AND needs a reveal-flash. Ice's is neither. Recipe: CGEvent.menuBarItemEvent(type,location,item,pid,source) = a normal CGEvent(mouseEventSource:.hidSystemState) with fields SET: .eventTargetUnixProcessID=ownerPID, .mouseEventWindowUnderMousePointer=windowID, .mouseEventWindowUnderMousePointerThatCanHandleThisEvent=windowID, .windowID=windowID, .eventSourceUserData=uniqueTag; .mouseEventClickState=1 for clicks; flags=.maskCommand on move-down only. The event is SELF-ADDRESSED to the item's window+process, so (a) location need NOT be over the item — works on OFF-SCREEN items (no reveal flash), (b) it bypasses the HID stream remote-desktop intercepts. Posted via scrombleEvent(from:.pid(ownerPID), to:.sessionEventTap): two EventTaps match the unique userData with a 50ms timeout to VERIFY each event landed (the reliability magic). MOVE = down(Cmd) at item frame + up at destination (MoveDestination.leftOfItem/rightOfItem). CLICK = down+up(.click, no Cmd, clickState=1). => Rebuild helper event layer on menuBarItemEvent + session-tap post + userData-verify; drop synthCmdDrag/CGWarpMouse. Replaces BOTH forwardClick and the park-drag; true single-item reveal, no flash, RD-immune.

title: Strategy C hide: move control NSStatusItem from helper to main app (ObjC interop)
description:
The Strategy-C hide mechanism (anchored control NSStatusItem, expand-to-hide) CANNOT run in the BevelHelper process: its hand-rolled NSApp.run() isn't a real app lifecycle, so every NSStatusBar/NSStatusItem operation deadlocks the status-bar IPC. Proven live (bevel-7hf4): toggling -> setHidden entered the main thread and never returned; creating at launch wedged the helper (Ping timeout -> killed). 

FIX: create + own the control item in the MAIN Bevel.App process (Avalonia hosts a real NSApplication run loop) via ObjC interop (Bevel.Interop; see the macos-inbound-apple-events dynamic-ObjC recipe). Wire the existing 'Consolidate the menu bar into the tray' setting (Tray tab) directly to an app-side NSStatusItem manager — expand length to 10000 to hide, variableLength to reveal, anchored via autosaveName + 'NSStatusItem Preferred Position' UserDefault (all proven in native/helper-macos/menubar-hide-poc.swift). No gRPC helper for the hide; the helper keeps doing tray-icon capture (F3). Then re-enable reveal-at-top (C2) against the app-side item. The helper-side control-item code (MenuBarControlItem, SetConsolidation RPC) is currently disabled/dead and should be removed or repurposed.

title: Restart: supervised child must not self-re-exec (dual-path race → orphan taskbar)
description: Trace (2026-08-09, live): on 'Restart Bevel', launcher correctly runs RestartAllAsync (respawns core+taskbar in-place), BUT the old taskbar ALSO hits RequestRestart's fallback: 'launcher-control send=False → this process re-execs itself standalone'. A launcher-supervised child (LauncherControl.IsSupervised==true, BEVEL_LAUNCHER_SOCKET set) must NEVER do the standalone in-place re-exec — that orphans a taskbar with no core (localhost:80 gRPC errors) and races the launcher's clean respawn → intermittent 'restart crashed'. FIX: in App.RequestRestart, if TrySend fails but IsSupervised, just RequestExit (let the launcher monitor respawn), NOT set _restartRequested/Relaunch. Standalone re-exec only when !IsSupervised. Diagnosed via RestartDiag instrumentation (src/Bevel.App/RestartDiag.cs).

title: Theme switch Luna→Win2000 doesn't re-chrome already-open windows (no borders, Luna title bar)
description:
Switching Luna→Win2000 leaves EXISTING windows borderless with a Luna-ish title bar; newly-opened windows are correct. Root cause (confirmed): Luna applies its window chrome via <Style> setters in the Luna Styles set (LunaTheme.axaml ~ll.1230-1241): (1) ':is(Window) /template/ classic|ClassicBorderDecorator#Bd' BorderThickness=0 (turns off the Classic 3D border so Luna's rounded frame shows), and (2) ':is(Window)' Background=Transparent + TransparencyLevelHint=Transparent (rounded-corner notch see-through). ThemeService.Apply removes the Luna Styles set on switch, and adding a Styles set re-templates live controls — but REMOVING one does NOT reliably re-evaluate template-part setters, and a macOS native window's transparency cannot be un-set live. So open windows keep border-off + transparency. All resource-level fixes (LunaVariantService.Clear via ThemeVariants.Apply — now wired at every switch site incl. SettingsWindow) are necessary but insufficient for this.
PROPOSED FIX: make the window-chrome differences TOKEN-DRIVEN so they revert on the token-dict swap instead of via a removable Style set — e.g. a permanent base style binding Bd.BorderThickness to a Bevel.Metric.WindowFrameBevel token (Luna=0, Win2000=Classic value) and Window.Background to a token. The native TransparencyLevelHint likely can't live-revert on macOS → either keep windows opaque-with-alpha-corners another way, or accept that the transparency aspect needs window recreation / a shell restart. Interim: restarting the shell after a theme switch yields fully-correct chrome (all windows recreated).
acceptance_criteria: After switching Luna→Win2000 live, already-open windows show the correct Classic 3D border and a Classic (non-Luna) title bar, without a restart — or, if the native-transparency limitation is unavoidable, the border+caption revert live and only the corner-transparency needs a documented restart.
notes: LIVE REPRO 2026-07-28 (full --role=launcher shell, dev-signed debug build): opened an Explorer under Luna Purple (confirmed glossy purple caption), then flipped themeId luna->win2000 via settings.db+version bump. RESULT: the open window re-chromed CORRECTLY — caption reverted from Luna purple to Win2000 blue with square Win2000 min/max/close buttons, toolbar went gray, borders intact. The taskbar ALSO re-chromed (Luna purple -> Win2000 gray). Reported symptom ('no borders, Luna title bar') did NOT occur in ANY window (standalone explorer, full-shell explorer, taskbar). Conclusion: appears RESOLVED in the current build — likely by the prior symmetric LunaVariantService.Clear()/ColorSchemeService.Clear() work. RECOMMEND: verify once more via the Settings UI toggle (not just DB) then close. Screenshots: /tmp/bevel-exp-luna.png (before) vs /tmp/bevel-exp-after.png (after).
close_reason: Live-disproved 2026-07-28: opened Explorer under Luna Purple, switched to Win2000 via settings — caption reverted to Win2000 blue + square buttons, toolbar gray, borders intact; taskbar also re-chromed correctly. Reported symptom (no borders / stuck Luna title bar) does not occur in the current build (fixed by prior symmetric LunaVariantService/ColorSchemeService Clear() work). Reopen if the native-transparency facet resurfaces.

title: Shell chrome tooltips leak into taskbar window list (split mode)
description:
In split-process mode the taskbar/desktop role processes ran macOS .regular activation policy, so their own transient popups (tooltips, menus) passed the Swift helper's window filter, got registered as foreign taskbar entries, shifted the bar, and the layout/focus churn dismissed the tooltips. The helper's reserved-title exclusion ('Bevel Taskbar'/'Bevel Desktop') never matched — the CG window title is the generic 'Avalonia Application'.

Fix: mark the taskbar and desktop role processes .accessory (NSApplicationActivationPolicyAccessory) at startup via new Bevel.Pal.MacOS.ShellActivation.HideFromDock(), called from App.OnFrameworkInitializationCompleted for ShellRole.Taskbar/Desktop. This is correct shell identity (no Dock tile, out of Cmd-Tab) AND makes the helper's existing activationPolicy==.regular filter drop ALL their windows (main + tooltips), title-independent. Not applied to All mode: that process also hosts the file-manager window, which should appear in the taskbar; activation policy can't distinguish it from a tooltip in the same process (needs window-level/subrole filtering instead).
notes: CORRECTION to earlier close: the .accessory change (ShellActivation.HideFromDock) did NOT fix the phantom-button/tooltip bug — it only affects the FILTERED snapshot path (describe) and shell Dock identity. Real root cause: the Swift helper's AX-observer event path (enqueueAXEvent -> buildTaskbarWindowFromAX -> broadcast) broadcast .opened for EVERY window an observed app created, bypassing describe()'s filters, so the shell's own .accessory tooltip/menu popups (a flood of empty-title 'Avalonia Application' windows) leaked as phantom taskbar buttons until the 2s snapshot reconcile pruned them. Fix: gate enqueueAXEvent on NSRunningApplication(pid).activationPolicy == .regular, mirroring describe(). Diagnosed via new BEVEL_DEBUG_TASKBAR=1 taskbar logging (176 phantom ADDs in one hover session). Also fixed: clock tooltip flicker (PlacementMode.Top so it isn't under the cursor).
close_reason: Fixed + live-verified. Taskbar/desktop role processes now set .accessory via ShellActivation.HideFromDock() in App.OnFrameworkInitializationCompleted. Verified on running split shell: lsappinfo reports both as type=UIElement; helper debug log shows 'drop ... Avalonia Application pid=<taskbar/desktop> reason=activationPolicy=1'; real foreign apps (Finder, Firefox, Chrome, Claude, ...) still kept; 0 errors.

title: Harden WindowServiceImpl.swift concurrency & observer lifecycle
description: Code review (swift-ios persona) flagged pre-existing thread-safety and lifecycle issues in native/helper-macos/Sources/BevelHelper/WindowServiceImpl.swift: (P1) unsynchronized mutation of lastForeignFrontmostPID; (P1) broadcast() does not actually serialize writer.write() despite the writeQueue/comment; (P1) AXObserver refcon passUnretained with no sync against in-flight callbacks during shutdown/deinit; (P2) Changes-stream subscribers never removed on client disconnect; (P2) per-instance NSWorkspace observer never removed; (P2) force-casts on CFTypeRef from third-party AX servers can crash the daemon; (P3) addObserver doesn't check isShutdown. Pre-existing (not this session), so out of the review's apply scope — filed for follow-up.
design: Serialize writer.write via the existing writeQueue (actual queue.sync/async, not just a comment); guard lastForeignFrontmostPID under stateLock; remove per-client subscribers on disconnect and the NSWorkspace observer on shutdown/deinit; replace force-casts (as!) on AX CFTypeRef with conditional casts + safe fallback; gate addObserver on isShutdown. Consider a TSan run in CI to catch the data races.
acceptance_criteria: No unsynchronized shared-state access (TSan clean on a representative session); writer.write serialized; observers/subscribers removed on disconnect/shutdown; AX value casts are non-crashing.
close_reason: All 7 findings fixed in WindowServiceImpl.swift (+339/-98); swift build clean + 33 tests 0 failures, independently re-verified. (1,P1) lastForeignFrontmostPID read-modify-write now inside a single stateLock.withLock block, lock released before any AX call. (2,P1) broadcast() serializes writer.write via writeQueue.async + DispatchSemaphore (ordered, one-at-a-time, no deadlock for on-queue callers). (3,P2) Changes subscribers removed on disconnect via defer+while(!Task.isCancelled). (4,P2) NSWorkspace didLaunch observer token captured + removed in shutdown/deinit. (5,P2) all five AX/CF force-casts replaced with CFGetTypeID guards + safe fallback so a hostile AX server can't crash the daemon. (6,P1) AXObserver refcon dangling-callback race closed: run-loop source removal marshalled onto the AX run-loop thread (performOnAXRunLoopSync) before CFRunLoopStop, teardown closure captures only locals. (7,P3) addObserver early-returns when isShutdown. Invariants preserved: describe() sole descriptor builder, isShellChrome layer-0 filter untouched.

title: Startup: defer the helper ScreenCaptureKit/AX tray self-test off the first-paint window
description: Measured: the Swift helper's tray self-test (ScreenCaptureKit + AX grant + liveMirroring) is ~1.3s to Ping-ready then ~4.8s more to 'liveMirroring=true', a ~5s 100%-CPU burst (t+2.5s..~8s) that overlaps taskbar paint and leaves the tray empty until it completes — the visible 'shell settles slowly / tray fills in late'. title: Automation socket (bevelctl / bevel://) only served by on-demand Explorer in split mode
description: After role=all removal (bevel-dwhy), AutomationSocketHost (CompositionRoot.cs ~195) is registered only for role=Explorer. In split mode Explorer is on-demand, so bevelctl and bevel:// URLs don't work until an Explorer window process exists — previously role=all always served it, so 'open this folder in Bevel' from outside worked cold. The Start menu / desktop still open folders (they call Program.SpawnExplorer directly, not via the socket), so daily UI use is fine; only EXTERNAL automation is degraded. Fix: serve the automation socket from a PERSISTENT process — the core (headless, already always-on) or the taskbar — and have its window verbs spawn/route to an Explorer via the launcher (SpawnExplorer / a launcher control command). Consider that IShellAutomation window verbs need the live file manager, so the persistent server may need to spawn an Explorer to fulfill window-coupled verbs.

title: Taskbar lags on macOS Space (desktop) switch — no activeSpaceDidChange observer
description: Switching macOS Spaces takes 'a few rounds' for the taskbar to show the right windows. Helper (WindowServiceImpl.swift) observes didLaunch/didActivate + per-window AX notifications but NOT NSWorkspace.activeSpaceDidChangeNotification, so a Space switch gives no signal and only the >=1s/2s reconcile backstop catches it. 'A few rounds' because a mid-animation enumeration reads a stale on-screen set. Fix: add an activeSpaceDidChangeNotification observer next to the didActivate/didLaunch ones (~1419-1435); on fire poke an immediate reconcile after a ~250-400ms settle (post-animation), debounced. Event-driven fix — do NOT shorten the global reconcile interval (battery). NSWorkspace observers deliver on the main thread — mind the AX-run-loop-thread note.
close_reason: Helper now observes NSWorkspace.activeSpaceDidChangeNotification and fires a single debounced reconcile() ~300ms post-animation (coalesced via cancel/replace DispatchWorkItem), reusing the poll's enumerate+diff+broadcast so the taskbar snaps to the new Space's windows instead of waiting for the 500ms backstop. Observer + work item torn down in shutdown(); [weak self]. Benign occasional overlap with the poll reconcile (self-healing). Subteam+verifier SOUND; helper builds; no .NET change. Commit bfd301a.

title: First window-minimize after granting Screen Recording hitches the UI (one-time warmup)
description:
User-observed: the FIRST time an Explorer window is minimized after Screen Recording is granted, the shell freezes briefly, then recovers and never recurs (confirmed: 2nd minimize instant; live sampling of the single-process role=all app showed the main thread idle in the event loop except for transient .NET JIT frames — genssStructReturn/fgMorphSmpOp/LinearScan::allocateRegisters — no sustained block, no deadlock).

Cause (inferred, not yet caught mid-freeze): first-run warmup on the UI thread — JIT of the minimize->taskbar-update->capture path + the first live ScreenCaptureKit init (initial SCShareableContent establishes a CGS/WindowServer connection, slow cold). Only surfaced now because Screen Recording was just granted, so live mirroring/thumbnail capture became active for the first time.

Fix: (1) audit the window-state-change / thumbnail-capture path (TaskbarView.CaptureWindowAsync @ ~675, ShellModel window-change handlers) to GUARANTEE no capture/enumeration/helper-RPC is awaited on the UI thread — it must be fully off-thread with only the cheap result marshaled back (ties to the audit's 'CaptureWindow RPC no timeout' findings). (2) Pre-warm ScreenCaptureKit off-thread right after the grant / at helper start (a throwaway SCShareableContent fetch) so the first real capture is warm. (3) Optionally warm the minimize path.

To catch the exact cold stack: fresh-restart Bevel (cold JIT) + prime a 2s-slice sampler + trigger the FIRST minimize; the blocking frame will show which call is on-thread.
close_reason: Pre-warm ScreenCaptureKit in the helper (detached, CGPreflight-gated so no prompt, retries for grant-after-start) so the first live capture isn't cold; added the missing intrinsic timeout to the window-capture RPC (MacOSWindowManager 3s, ShellCoreWindowManager 5s, Swift-side timeout) with static-icon fallback — also resolves the audit's 'CaptureWindow RPC no timeout' finding. Root cause was first-run warmup (JIT + cold SCK CGS init), not a deadlock. Subteam: investigate+implement+2 verifiers SOUND. 802 tests green, Swift helper builds, notarized bundle installed to /Applications.

title: Tab provider: Gecko dialect (Zen, Firefox) via accessibility — enumerate + AXPress activation
description:
Extend bevel-a40b's ITabProvider to Firefox-family browsers, verified live on the Studio against Zen (app.zen-browser.zen, 86-tab session) 2026-08-17:

- AppleScript is a dead end: Zen/Firefox expose the basic suite only — 'tab' is not a class in the dictionary (script fails to compile). The existing osascript path cannot serve this family.
- AX is the lever: every tab (including Zen's vertical sidebar) is an AXRadioButton, subrole AXTabButton, roleDescription 'tab', inside an AXTabGroup, with actions AXShowMenu/AXScrollToVisible/AXPress. AXPress switches the tab. Titles match the session store exactly. Probe source: scratchpad ax_probe.swift (this session).
- Session store recovery.jsonlz4 (mozLz4: 'mozLz40\0' magic + LE u32 size + LZ4 block) in the profile gives titles+URLs+pinned+selected promptlessly (~15 s freshness), but ordering vs the AX strip is not guaranteed across pinned tabs/workspaces.

Design: enumerate AND activate from the SAME source (AX) so tab indices can never disagree — walk app windows → AXTabGroup → AXTabButton children (title, window index, tab index); ActivateAsync re-walks and AXPresses by index (title-guarded). URLs stay null like the iTerm dialect (or optionally enrich titles from the session store by title match). Implementation seat: either C# P/Invoke of the AX C API alongside the existing ObjC interop in Bevel.Pal.MacOS (all roles share the pl.ikari.bevel AX grant), or a helper RPC — decide at build time. Update SupportsApp declines-firefox/zen tests to the new expectation.
close_reason: Shipped: GeckoTabEngine (AX enumerate + AXPress activate) verified live against Zen (84 tabs, round-trip); Opus review HIGHs fixed (truncation-safe press policy, CF type guards, interop cache races); deferred items in bevel-y3cl.

title: Hide mirrored icons from the macOS menu bar when Bevel owns them (Bartender-style)
description: User: when Bevel's tray owns/mirrors a menu-bar icon, also HIDE it from the macOS menu bar (de-duplicate), like Bartender/Ice. macOS has NO public API to hide another app's NSStatusItem. Approaches: (a) our own wide NSStatusItem that expands to push the others off the visible bar (Bartender/Ice technique) — helper-side, fragile across macOS versions + the notch; (b) Accessibility-driven manipulation. Sizable helper feature; needs its own TCC + live validation. Natural extension of the existing tray live-mirror (TrayServiceImpl). Design first: which icons to hide (owned/mirrored set), a reveal affordance, and the collapse mechanism.
notes: OVERLAY-HIDE proven viable (subteam design + PoC): a click-through borderless panel at level 26 covers the status-item strip; occluded-on-display items KEEP REDRAWING (PoC: clock id=14 prints CHANGED every 1s), fixing the live-updates freeze that off-screen push caused. Also makes clicks land directly (items never move) and retires the control NSStatusItem. NEXT: implement src/Bevel.Pal.MacOS/MacMenuBarOverlay.cs (mirror MacMenuBarControl; NSPanel via ObjC; frame = the mirrored tray items' x-range so the clock/Control-Center stay visible; ignoresMouseEvents; opaque menu-bar-matching bg), add NSRect-passing objc_msgSend + window setters to AppKitInterop.cs, swap MacOSSystemTrayHost.SetNativeTrayHiddenAsync to it (keep MacMenuBarControl off-screen push behind a per-app fallback flag). title: Tray live-mirror icons go stale / don't rebuild
description: User: tray icons often don't rebuild. Path: TrayServiceImpl live-mirrors menu-bar icons via ScreenCaptureKit on the 2s poll + diff; captureWindow returning empty PNG is intentionally dropped (:394) so the last-good icon sticks. So symptom = capture returns empty/stale (SCK reliability: window-id churn, throttling, or the item moved) and the stale icon persists. Runtime-only diagnosis (can't repro headless). Instrument captureWindow (log empty vs ok, item id/x/width, cadence) + consider: force a recapture on a longer heartbeat, invalidate on x/width change, or fall back to the app icon after N empties. Related: bevel-tnii (redundant 2s full re-ship).
notes: REFINED from a live screenshot: it's not stale-but-real icons — EVERY tray item renders the same generic placeholder square. So IconPng is coming through as a generic fallback (capture empty -> owning-app icon -> a default), not real menu-bar bytes. TrayViewModel.IconSource = TrayIconTint.Process(item.IconPng). Root issue is the SCK capture-mirror producing placeholders for ~all items. This weakens the whole capture-mirror model; see bevel-7hf4 (Ice-style hide) as the better direction — the user pointed there.

InfoPane.axaml has ~20+ hexes incl. a drawn file-icon illustration; each needs a semantic-vs-fixed judgment (which values dark-mode/accent should derive vs fixed illustration geometry). Best done AS PART OF the derivation engine (bevel-fdo5) so tokens map to real derivation inputs, not invented ad hoc. Clean sub-win available anytime: ItemView FontSize=11 literals -> one shared font token.

title: Fix Win2000 window-border geometry regression (a967ec8)
description: Commit a967ec8 (fix(luna): title bar is the rounded top of the frame) restructured third_party/classic-avalonia/.../Styles/Window.axaml so the caption docks full-bleed. Two Win2000 breaks despite the "verified unchanged by render" claim: (1) lost the 4px sizing frame — removed RootLayout Margin=4 so caption abuts the Bd bevel (no 2px face strip); (2) lost the 1px caption→client separator (removed AutoAttachTitleBar Margin=0,0,0,1) so the band is 4px not 1px. Fix: add Bevel.Metric.CaptionMargin token (Win2000 4,4,4,0 / Luna 0) bound in Window.axaml; change Win2000 WindowContentInset 4 → 4,1,4,4; regen via tools/ThemeGen; add the headless pixel-sampling render test a967ec8 lacked. Keep Luna full-bleed unchanged.
close_reason: Closed

title: Start-menu inline search: type-ahead results panel (apps, files, tabs) — the search foundation
description: A type-to-search experience inside the Start menu itself (XP Vista+ style, rendered in the classic skin): focus lands in a search field when the Start menu opens (or on first keystroke), results replace/overlay the menu body in ranked sections — Programs (InstalledApps, already enumerated for the Start menu), Files (VFS), and later Tabs (bevel-vtc6) and Settings. Enter activates top hit; arrows navigate. Non-blocking: query providers async off-thread with a snapshot cache, marshal results back (NEVER block UI thread). Existing Start > Search (bevel-x6pv, Explorer Find mode) stays as the 'Find Files...' verb. This is the foundation bead-vtc6 and future search providers plug into — design the provider seam (ISearchProvider?) so sections are pluggable.

title: Start-menu search over tabs: type-to-jump across every ITabProvider app
description: Feed ITabProvider (bevel-a40b) into Start > Search: search all running supported apps' tabs by title+URL (parallel GetTabsAsync, ~200ms budget, cache last snapshot for instant first paint), rank by match quality, Enter activates the tab via ActivateAsync. Surfaces as a 'Tabs' section in search results alongside apps/files. The killer 'designed in 2026' feature: no classic shell ever searched inside apps' tabs.

title: Tabs menu favicons: Chromium Favicons DB + iTerm session colors as row icons
description: Tab rows in the task-button menu (bevel-a40b) show real site icons. Chromium family: per-profile 'Favicons' SQLite keyed by page URL — copy-then-query (live DB is locked), decode smallest >=16px bitmap, cache via the icon pipeline (respect NEVER-block-UI + vector/AA conventions; favicons are external content, exempt from vector-only as raster sources like app icons are). Arc profile dir: ~/Library/Application Support/Arc/User Data/Default. iTerm: no favicons — use per-session tab color/badge from its AppleScript dictionary instead. Safari favicon cache is TCC-protected (~/Library/Safari, needs FDA) — out of scope.
notes: Verified live on the Studio 2026-08-17: (1) Arc's Chromium Favicons DB (~/Library/Application Support/Arc/User Data/Default/Favicons): icon_mapping(page_url)→favicon_bitmaps join returns 16x16 PNGs directly (1436 bitmaps; blob magic 89504E47). Copy-then-query works while Arc runs. (2) ZEN TOO — extend scope beyond Chromium: profile favicons.sqlite (moz_pages_w_icons→moz_icons_to_pages→moz_icons join by page URL; 867 icons, 16px rows are PNG blobs). Gecko wrinkle: AX tab rows carry no URL, so the Zen/Firefox half needs the session-store title→URL enrichment from bevel-y3cl first; the Chromium half is independent (tab URLs already in AppTab.Url).

title: Arc tabs menu: prefer live/recent tabs over raw sidebar order (Space-aware)
description: v1 (bevel-a40b) lists Arc tabs in scripting-model order — Arc's single AppleScript window aggregates the whole sidebar (every Space's pinned + Today tabs, 182 on the reference machine), so the 25-row menu cap surfaces pinned sidebar items rather than what the user perceives as 'open tabs'. Improve ranking/filtering: (a) parse ~/Library/Application Support/Arc/StorableSidebar.json (promptless, no TCC) to identify loaded/recently-active tabs and the Space structure; (b) prefer live tabs first, then recency; (c) optionally group menu rows by Space with separators. Keep the AE path for activation (sidebar JSON has no activation verb). Related: firefox/zen session-file provider from the same design discussion.

title: Apphost links /opt/homebrew brotli — breaks portability of signed builds
description: Both Bevel and bevelctl apphosts link /opt/homebrew/opt/brotli/lib/libbrotli{dec,enc}.1.dylib because the .NET SDK is Homebrew-installed (its singlefilehost is built against brew brotli). Consequences: (1) deploys fail on Macs without brew brotli at that exact path; (2) under hardened runtime, library validation rejects the brew lib (Team ID mismatch) unless disable-library-validation is granted — worked around 2026-08-06 by signing nested executables with the app entitlements in sign-app.sh. Root fix: build release artifacts with the official Microsoft .NET SDK (or bundle brotli and rewrite install names with install_name_tool), then the entitlement workaround for bevelctl can be dropped.

title: Empty Trash + Restore/Put Back UI for the Trash view
description: TrashProvider (bevel-sw3k) makes Trash browsable + per-item permanent delete works via the existing Delete action. Follow-ups: (1) an 'Empty Trash' entry (folder-background menu + File menu) that permanently deletes all children, behind a confirmation dialog (irreversible). (2) 'Restore'/'Put Back': restore-to-chosen-folder via TrashMutator.MoveAsync exists; true Put-Back to the original location needs per-item metadata macOS doesn't expose for arbitrary trashed items — would require Bevel to write freedesktop-style .trashinfo sidecars at trash time (touch LocalFsProvider.LocalTrash.MoveToTrash). (3) show 'Restore' in the item context menu only when scheme==trash.
notes: Confirmed no reusable confirm dialog exists (would hand-build one). Restore also needs a FolderPickerDialog + VFS move out of trash. Core op is IRREVERSIBLE (permanent delete-all) — implement carefully at the start of a session, not rushed. Scope stands: (1) Empty Trash in folder-BG + File menu when folder scheme==trash, behind a real confirmation dialog; (3) Restore item in BuildItemMenu when node scheme==trash. Defer (2) true Put-Back (.trashinfo sidecars).

title: Automation control socket has file-perm-only auth (no nonce), unlike helper/shell-core
description: AutomationSocket accept loop (src/Bevel.Interop/Cli/AutomationSocket.cs:133) authenticates nothing and relies solely on 0600/0700, yet it exposes equally destructive verbs (delete/move/make) that the gRPC + shell-core channels protect with an HMAC nonce. Fix: layer the same per-session nonce on this channel. Related: bevel-kyf (peer-UID), bevel-twq (AE auth).

title: The .beveltheme package pipeline / third-party themes are unimplemented
description: ThemeService (src/Bevel.UI/ThemeService.cs:34) is a hardcoded 3-entry array with switch-based Source/StylesFor; there is no IThemeService, ThemeDescriptor, user-themes dir, manifest, or InstallPackageAsync anywhere. The spec .beveltheme zip format (05-theming section 2, THM-01..04) is entirely absent. Fix: implement the package format, import flow, and user themes directory. Related: bevel-dob.

title: Taskbar process spawn is serialized behind full core readiness
description: RoleProcessSupervisor.StartAllInOrderLocked (src/Bevel.App/Supervision/RoleProcessSupervisor.cs:145) awaits coreReadyProbe before forking the taskbar, so launcher->bar-visible = core cold start + helper connect + socket bind, THEN the taskbar cold start, fully serial — even though the taskbar client already retries connect (ShellModel.cs:499). Fix: spawn the taskbar immediately after core and let its client retry, overlapping the two cold starts. Split-mode (--role=launcher) only.
close_reason: RoleProcessSupervisor now spawns roles back-to-back (order preserved) and awaits core readiness AFTER, so the taskbar cold start overlaps the core's. Committed e351dfd; live-verified full shell boots (launcher+core+taskbar+helper).

title: Cold Explorer window does a wasted double-navigation (Home then target)
description: FileManagerWindowFactory.cs:57 SetController navigates to Home, then :61 navigates to the real start directory; the dedup at FileManagerController.cs:92 only no-ops when target==Home, so a places-spawned explorer kicks off a Home enumeration that is immediately superseded — wasted cold I/O on the fresh window first paint. Fix: pass the start directory into SetController so only one navigation fires.
close_reason: SetController now takes an optional start dir and navigates once; factory reordered to set view mode then single-nav. No wasted Home enumeration. Tested. Committed.

title: Redundant 2s full-ListWindows poll re-ships every window icon on top of the delta stream
description:
Redundant 2s full-ListWindows poll re-ships every window icon on top of the delta stream.

READY-TO-IMPLEMENT PLAN (Option A, icons-optional ListWindows) — scoped 2026-07-28, needs Swift toolchain (protoc-gen-swift) + a helper rebuild + an UNLOCKED session to live-validate icon behaviour:
- The waste: ShellModel.ReconcileLoopAsync (src/Bevel.Taskbar/Model/ShellModel.cs:163-184, ReconcileInterval=2s @ :291) calls _windows.EnumerateAsync → MacOSWindowManager.EnumerateAsync (MacOSWindowManager.cs:72-86) → helper ListWindows, which ALWAYS includes appIconPng (WindowServiceImpl.swift describe() :506-508). Reconcile (ShellModel.cs:197-241) only uses Id/Title/IsFocused/IsMinimized — never icons. Decode/render is already mitigated (icon cache + FNV-1a64 dedup; update path never touches IconSource). Remaining waste = IPC serialize/transfer + per-window ToByteArray() (MacOSWindowManager.cs:278) every 2s.
- Fix: add 'bool include_icons = N;' to ListWindowsRequest in proto/bevel.helper.v1.proto (default true keeps other callers). C# regenerates via Grpc.Tools on build. Run native/helper-macos/generate-proto.sh for the Swift .pb.swift. In describe()/enumerateWindows() skip win.appIconPng when !include_icons. MacOSWindowManager.EnumerateAsync sets include_icons=false for the reconcile poll (ShellModel is its only caller). Rebuild helper (build.sh).
- Trade-off: a window first surfaced BY the poll (a genuinely missed Opened delta) is icon-less until the next real delta — rare (helper's 500ms reconcile emits Opened WITH icons). Option B (per-window icon_hash gate) survives that but is more plumbing.
- Overlaps bevel-8ck (FIXED): the core also double-snapshots the tray. Same 'delta + periodic keyed reconcile carrying only identity, never heavy blobs' pattern as bevel-6nve.
notes: Assessed this session: the 2s reconcile backstop is a deliberate safety net (prunes a stale button from a missed Close that the Changes stream can't guarantee). The 're-ships icons' cost is PAYLOAD only — the helper caches icons per bundle-id so it doesn't re-RENDER, it just re-sends ~1KB/window every 2s (masked by the 16MB gRPC limit). The proper fix (id-only liveness enumeration on the reconcile path) needs a new lightweight helper RPC (ListWindowIds) — proto + Swift helper + client + regen + live validation. Marginal value vs cross-layer cost; deferred. NOT a quick interval bump (that would weaken the stale-button backstop).

title: Settings cross-process propagation is a wasteful 750ms full-blob poll; make it push
description: Every process runs a 750ms DispatcherTimer calling ReloadIfChangedAsync; ReadRowAsync (src/Bevel.Core/SettingsService.cs:228) always SELECTs the ENTIRE json blob just to compare a version int, and the timer defeats App Nap/idle (battery). Also App.axaml.cs:278 only wires FrequentCap on Changed, so most live settings do not reach a split-mode taskbar without restart. Fix (cheap): SELECT version first, fetch json only when it advanced. Fix (right): FSEvents watch on settings.db-wal or push via the shell-core CoreEvent broadcast, and fan every setting through ApplyLiveSettings cross-process.
notes: SHIPPED (6d6d940): version-probe — the 750ms poll now SELECTs only the version int on the no-change tick instead of the whole JSON blob (the core waste). PUSH ATTEMPTED + REVERTED this session: a FileSystemWatcher on the settings DB fired reliably for DIRECT file writes but NOT for SQLite's WAL write path (verified — direct write = 6 events, SQLite UpdateAsync = 0 within 5s), so a watcher-based push would MISS and regress propagation to the fallback interval. A reliable push needs the shell-core CoreEvent broadcast (the doc's original plan): writer signals core -> core broadcasts settings-changed -> UI processes reload. That's a cross-process feature, deferred. Poll stays at 750ms (cheap now).
close_reason: Core (and all-in-one) is now the SOLE opener+writer of settings.db; Taskbar/Explorer/Desktop use RemoteSettingsService (never touch SQLite) — snapshot on connect + SettingsChanged broadcast on write, RFC-7386 merge patches forwarded to core as sole writer, version-dedup, defaults-fallback startup. 750ms poll retired + CAS collapsed. role=all provably IPC-free. Split-taskbar tray-empty regression (shared client ate the on-connect TraySnapshot) fixed via a dedicated keyed 'settings' client. Subteam + 2 verifiers; 818 tests green. Commit 264f84f.

title: Settings load blocks first paint; parallelize startup
description: Program.cs:73 does SettingsService.LoadAsync().GetAwaiter().GetResult() (SQLite open+WAL+table-create+deserialize) serially before StartWithClassicDesktopLifetime, and ThemeService.Apply builds theme dictionaries synchronously on the paint thread per process. Fix: kick LoadAsync in parallel with BuildAvaloniaApp() and await at the first consumer (theme apply); consider a tiny theme+font fast-read split from the full blob.
close_reason: SettingsService.LoadAsync now kicked off-thread right after the Core early-return, overlapping SQLite open+parse with BuildAvaloniaApp()+host.Start(); awaited before StartWith (before dispatcher pumps). Committed e351dfd; live-verified clean boot.

title: No real thumbnails or OS file icons (IconResolver is a stub)
description: IconResolver.cs:56 returns null; Icons/Details/Thumbnails all render the same hand-drawn vector glyphs and Thumbnails view is just a 96px glyph. Fix: off-thread image/thumbnail + native-icon pipeline (cached), keep vector glyphs as fallback.

title: Symlinks: no reparse detection or cycle guard (recursion risk)
description: LocalFsProvider.cs:68 classifies purely on FileAttributes.Directory with no ReparsePoint detection; LocalTrash.CopyDirectory:440 recurses with no symlink check, so trashing/copying a tree with a directory symlink can follow it (infinite recursion / out-of-tree copy). Fix: detect reparse points, do not follow dir symlinks when copying, guard cycles.
close_reason: CopyDirectory now recreates symlinks via LinkTarget/CreateSymbolicLink instead of following them; cycle test terminates. Committed.

title: Trash is not browsable; net:// and trash:// tree nodes throw
description: FileManagerWindow.axaml.cs:466 adds net:// and trash:// roots but FileManagerModule registers only LocalFsProvider+ComputerProvider, so selecting them throws KeyNotFoundException (swallowed). Deletes go to ~/.Trash yet there is no way to browse it. Fix: add a Trash VFS provider (list/restore/empty); implement or hide the network node.
close_reason: Closed

title: File-operation failures are invisible (Debug.WriteLine only)
description: RunOpAsync/PasteAsync/UndoFromUiAsync/NewFolderAsync in FileManagerWindow.axaml.cs route every error/partial failure to Debug.WriteLine, so in Release a half-failed paste or permission-denied delete looks like success. Fix: surface operation errors via a dialog or the status bar.
close_reason: Fixed + tested: LoadDirectory catches fs enumeration errors -> status bar; file-op failures -> modal MessageDialog. Committed.

title: Explorer: Tools → Folder Options opens the whole app Settings (theme/appearance) instead of folder/view options
description: FileManagerWindow wires Tools → 'Folder Options...' to open the full app SettingsWindow (theme, shell-enabled, show-hidden). So users get theme controls that change the ENTIRE theme when they expected folder view options. Real Windows 'Folder Options' is a focused dialog (View: show hidden/extensions/etc., General: single vs double click, etc.). TACKLE: build a dedicated Folder Options dialog (or a folder-scoped section) exposing view/behaviour options — move the app-wide theme/appearance to the Properties/Settings entry only. File: src/Bevel.FileManager/FileManagerWindow.axaml.cs ~209.
acceptance_criteria: Tools → Folder Options opens folder/view options (not the global theme picker); theme switching stays in the dedicated Settings/Properties surface.
close_reason: Implemented in 00ea027 (dialog + wired show-hidden/hide-extensions/default-view) + 6c0eea7 (selectable info-panel style Win2000/WinXP/Win9x/Off). Tools → Folder Options now opens a focused folder/view dialog, not the app theme picker; theme lives on taskbar Properties. All options functional (no dead controls); live cross-window apply; 591 tests green.

title: Start menu: unify shell-management actions + fix Luna 'Log Off' mislabel
description: Cross-theme parity gap. Win2000 Start menu has explicit Bevel-specific items 'Restart Bevel' (OnRestartClick→_restart) and 'Quit Bevel' (OnQuitClick→_quit). Luna has NEITHER as explicit items — instead it OVERLOADS the XP footer: 'Log Off' → _restart (MISLABEL: Log Off performs a restart) and 'Turn Off' → _quit. So the same shell actions are labelled inconsistently across themes and Luna's 'Log Off' is misleading. TACKLE: define one shell-action set (restart-shell, quit-shell) surfaced in both layouts with honest labels — e.g. Luna footer 'Restart' + 'Quit' (or keep XP wording but map Log Off→a real log-off/lock and Turn Off→quit), and ensure Win2000's Restart/Quit Bevel and Luna's footer invoke the same handlers. Aligns with 'designed in 2026': functional extensions are good, but labels must be truthful.
acceptance_criteria: Restart and Quit shell actions exist in BOTH themes with accurate labels; no button does something other than its label says.
notes: Partly done in f45348f: added explicit honest 'Restart Bevel' / 'Quit Bevel' rows to the Luna right column (parity with Win2000). REMAINING: the Luna footer 'Log Off' still calls _restart and 'Turn Off' calls _quit (kept per user's 'footer unchanged' choice) — the words still don't match a shell's actions. Options: relabel footer, or wire real session log-off/lock.

title: Implement the Flat (Whistler watercolor) theme from the design spec
description: Design spec ready at docs/design/flat/flat-theme-spec.md (+ swatches.html) — a watercolor 'designed in 2026' third identity: matte pastel washes, warm-cream/lilac-mist neutrals, aqua/coral/sage pigments, DARK ink text on light chrome (vs Win2000 white-on-navy, Luna white-on-blue). Implement per the spec: promote 'flat' from a token-only stub to a full Styles-set theme (FlatTokens.axaml + FlatTheme.axaml, wired via ThemeService.StylesFor like Luna), add the 'Flat' metrics column to theme.json, author the Bevel.Theme.* ControlThemes + caption wiring, and (per spec) promote the hardcoded Luna.Brush.StartMenu* keys to a theme-neutral Bevel.Brush.StartMenu* contract so both Luna and Flat can supply the two-column Start menu (StartMenu.axaml.cs layout switch currently hardcodes == luna). Keep AA on, vectors only.
acceptance_criteria: Selecting the Flat theme yields a coherent, distinct watercolor look across window chrome, controls, taskbar, and a properly-skinned Start menu — matching the spec; not a Win2000 clone.

title: Start menu: wire up or hide the dead menu items
description:
Audit found many Start-menu items that are no-op stubs (Click handler only calls Close()), which reads as broken:
- Win2000 (ClassicLayout): Help, Run…, Log Off…, Shut Down… — all just close.
- Luna: places (My Documents/Pictures/Music/Computer → OnLunaPlaceClick), Help (OnLunaHelpClick), Search (OnLunaSearchClick), Run (OnLunaRunClick) — all just close.
(Fixed already in commit 3113bb5: Luna pinned apps now actually launch via LaunchCommand.)
Working today: Settings/Control Panel → _openSettings; Programs cascade; Luna Turn Off → quit; Restart/Quit Bevel.
TACKLE: either implement (Run dialog, Search, places → open in file manager at the folder, Help → docs/about) OR hide/disable until implemented so the menu never shows dead entries. Recommend: places → open file manager (cheap, high value); Run → a real run dialog (feature); Search → later; hide Help until there's a target. Decide per-item implement-vs-hide.
acceptance_criteria: No Start-menu item is a silent no-op: each either performs a real action or is hidden/disabled with intent.
notes: Partly done in f45348f: Luna places (My Documents/Pictures/Music/Computer) now open Bevel Explorer; Luna pinned-app launch fixed (was double-launching). STILL dead stubs: Luna Help/Search/Run; Win2000 Help/Run/Log Off/Shut Down. Decide implement-vs-hide per item.
close_reason: Closed

title: SPIKE: represent running-but-windowless apps in the taskbar (macOS dock-dot concept)
description:
Our taskbar is window-centric (button per window). A macOS app can be RUNNING with zero windows (closed all, didn't quit; document app between documents) — dock shows a running dot, clicking reopens a window (applicationShouldHandleReopen). Today such an app has NO taskbar button -> invisible + unreachable from the bar.

SPIKE FIRST: instrument how often this happens in practice and for which apps (real daily pain vs rare) before committing to UI.

OPTIONS:
- A. Nothing (current).
- B. (recommended) App-presence buttons: helper diffs NSWorkspace.runningApplications (regular/dock activation-policy only) vs AX windows; a windowless-running app gets a distinct app button (icon, no title, dimmer). Click -> activate/reopen -> app makes a window -> becomes a normal window button.
- C. Full pinned+running model (Windows-7 style) — natural home for app-usage auto-pinning (bevel-xrx6).

EDGE CASES: filter to regular activation-policy apps (exclude accessory/menu-bar agents — some already appear in the systray mirror); exclude Bevel itself; handle the merge transition (app opens a window -> app button becomes the window button, no duplicate).

RELATED: bevel-xrx6 (frequency-based app suggestions) — consider a unified 'app-level taskbar entry' (pinned / running-windowless / window-group).
acceptance_criteria: Spike measures frequency + apps affected; decision recorded (do nothing vs app-presence buttons vs fold into a pinned model); if B, click-to-reopen works and the app button merges cleanly when a window appears.
notes:
Spike done (commit 46d755e): diagnostic found 13/24 regular apps windowless right now (54%) — real daily pain, NOT edge case. CGWindowList .optionAll is useless here (reports scaffolding windows); AX kAXWindows is authoritative → detector must live in the helper. Recommendation: Option B (app-presence buttons) as first slice of C, keyed by BUNDLE ID, modelled as the zero-window state of the app's existing TaskGroup so the merge transition (window opens/closes) is an in-place group update, no duplicate. activateWindow already falls back to NSRunningApplication.activate() for the reopen. Findings: docs/spec/spike-ww71-windowless-apps.md.
SHIPPED (commit 4a6a323, on top of 5824fea): windowless apps appear as reopen buttons + full app-centric context menu (app header, Windows submenu with per-window Activate/Minimize/Close, Quit/Force-Quit). App-level TerminateApp threaded proto→helper→PAL→IPC→VM; ForeignWindow.BundleId added. Dismiss via native NSEvent global mouse-down monitor (non-activating window defeats Avalonia light-dismiss). Force Quit is DECIDE-AT-OPEN (Option held at right-click, read via NSEvent.modifierFlags) — live in-place relabel proved impossible (MenuFlyout popup doesn't repaint after settling). 583 tests green.

title: Perf benchmark harness for frequent taskbar/shell operations
description:
Measure + guard the hot paths so perf doesn't regress silently.

STEP 0 (profile first): a dotnet-trace pass under real churn (rapid window open/close, theme switch, row drag, tray updates) to confirm the REAL hot spots before benchmarking guesses.

LIKELY HOT PATHS:
- Taskbar button reflow — TaskbarLayout width plan (pure fn, already testable); fires on every window add/remove/resize/row change.
- Tray — TrayIconTint.Process (per capture), TrayRowsPanel.AssignRows.
- Theme apply — ThemeService.Apply + LunaVariantService.Apply (Styles-set swap + resource re-inject).
- Settings serialize — SerializeRaw (every change).
- Icon geometry — Glyphs / ToolbarIcons vector build.
- IPC round-trips (taskbar<->core<->helper) — measured separately (I/O, not BDN).

TOOLING: a benchmarks/Bevel.Benchmarks BenchmarkDotNet project for the pure-CPU paths. BDN is too noisy to gate CI on absolute numbers -> two-tier guard: (a) BDN + committed baseline for local tracking; (b) a few lightweight 'budget' xUnit tests for worst cases (e.g. plan 50 buttons < N ms, tint 32px icon < M ms) that catch gross regressions without runner flakiness. Baselines in docs/perf.md.
acceptance_criteria: dotnet-trace profile identifies the top hot paths; Bevel.Benchmarks covers them with committed baselines; budget tests guard the top 2-3; docs/perf.md records numbers.
notes: Done (commit 442b6f8): benchmarks/Bevel.Benchmarks (BenchmarkDotNet, ShortRun, not in sln/CI) + PerfBudgetTests (CI-gated tripwires) + docs/perf.md. Baselines (Apple Silicon): ComputeButtonLayout ~1.3ns (O(1)), grouped Plan(100 windows) ~8.3µs, TrayRowsPanel.AssignRows 200x3 ~418ns, TrayIconTint.Process 32px ~16µs, SettingsService.SaveAsync ~199µs — none a bottleneck. Icon-geometry benchmark dropped: Avalonia Control build needs the UI thread BDN lacks. Not covered (need live harness/dotnet-trace): theme apply, taskbar reflow end-to-end, IPC round-trips.

title: On-device QA: tray adaptive tinting + multi-row/stacked-date
description:
Tray rework (commit 3284e52) is unit-tested for logic (TrayIconTint, TrayRowsPanel) but the LIVE rendering with real captured menu-bar icons needs on-device eyes:
(a) template-glyph tinting reads correctly across Luna colour variants (Blue/Silver/Black/Purple) + Win2000 — dark ink on bright bars, light on dark; colourful / self-contained icons left untouched.
(b) dragging to 2 rows produces 2 rows of tray icons at NATURAL widths (a wide status item takes proportional room, not uniform-to-widest).
(c) the clock date stacks under the time on a multi-row bar; inline on a single row.
acceptance_criteria: All three confirmed visually on-device; file follow-ups for any heuristic mis-detection (e.g. a colourful icon that gets tinted, or a mono icon that doesn't).

title: Frequency-based app suggestions: exclude-open filter + OS usage seeding
description:
## Motivation

Make the Start menu's frequent column (and future taskbar pins) genuinely useful by (a) surfacing the
apps the user actually launches most, weighted toward ones **not currently open** (already-running apps
don't need a launch shortcut), and (b) making that column **warm on first run** by seeding from the OS's
own usage history instead of starting empty until Bevel has accumulated its own launch data.

## Current state (what already exists)

- `ProgramUsageStore` (src/Bevel.Taskbar/Model/ProgramUsageStore.cs) — Bevel's own per-app launch
  frequency/recency tracking, persisted.
- `ShellModel` (src/Bevel.Taskbar/Model/ShellModel.cs) — computes the `Frequent` list capped by
  `FrequentCap` (the `TaskbarStartMenuFrequentCount` setting), with a `NewlyAddedWindow` recency window.
- The Luna Start menu already renders a frequent/pinned left column.
- The helper already provides the live open-window list (so "currently open" is known to `ShellModel`).

So the frequency *tracking* and *rendering* exist. This bead adds two things on top: an exclude/deprioritize-open
filter, and optional OS usage seeding.

## Scope

### Part A — "frequent among not-currently-open" filter
- `ShellModel.RecomputeFrequent` should optionally exclude (or strongly deprioritize) apps that currently
  have an open window, so the frequent column suggests apps to *launch*, not ones already running.
- Behaviour toggle in settings (`TaskbarStartMenuFrequentExcludeOpen`, default on) — some users may prefer
  the raw frequency list.
- Edge: an app that's frequent AND open shouldn't leave a gap — backfill from the next-most-frequent
  not-open app so the column stays full to `FrequentCap`.

### Part B — OS usage seeding (warm start)
- A one-time (or periodic-reconcile) seed of `ProgramUsageStore` from the OS's usage history, so a fresh
  install shows sensible frequent apps immediately. Bevel's own tracking takes over from there (seed only
  fills gaps / initial weights; never overwrites a higher Bevel-observed count).
- New PAL seam: `IUsageProvider` in Bevel.Pal.Abstractions returning `(bundleId/appPath, lastUsed, count?)`
  records, implemented per platform; no-op default so it degrades gracefully where unavailable.

## Per-platform seed mechanism

- **macOS**: Spotlight metadata `kMDItemLastUsedDate` (reliable, **no special permission**) via
  `MDQuery`/`mdls` over `/Applications` + user app dirs. `kMDItemUseCount` also exists but is mostly-null
  on recent macOS — treat as best-effort only. **Rejected**: `knowledgeC.db` (real per-app usage duration,
  but needs Full Disk Access + undocumented, schema-fragile across OS versions) — not worth the fragility.
- **Windows**: `UserAssist` registry keys (HKCU\...\Explorer\UserAssist, ROT13-encoded) — launch counts +
  last-used. This is the source the XP/7 Start-menu MFU itself used.
- **Linux**: Zeitgeist activity log (`~/.local/share/zeitgeist`) or `~/.local/share/recently-used.xbel`;
  best-effort, less standardized.

## Non-goals

- No real-time OS usage streaming (macOS has no public Screen Time read API; DeviceActivity is sandboxed).
- No usage *duration* tracking — launch frequency + recency only.
- Not changing the pinned (explicitly user-pinned) list semantics; this is the *frequent/suggested* column.

## Privacy

- Seeding reads local OS usage history only; nothing leaves the machine. Gate it behind a setting
  (`TaskbarSeedUsageFromOS`, default on for macOS Spotlight since it needs no permission; consider default
  off where a permission/gated store would be involved). Document what's read in the Properties dialog blurb.

title: M1: per-capability RPC auth scoping for helper services (ScriptingService/InputService)
description: M0's helper exposes only SupervisionService (Ping), gated by the per-session nonce — one token grants everything. M1 adds ScriptingService (Apple Events) and InputService (synthetic input), which are strictly more dangerous; a single all-or-nothing token means any code that can read the token (or any future in-proc plugin) gets input synthesis for free. Implement the capability-scoped design from bevel-vgg (see design field) before those services ship.
design:
Design (bevel-vgg item 3, 2026-07-10):
1. TOKEN FORMAT: keep one 16-byte session nonce as the MAC key, but per-RPC auth becomes 'x-bevel-token: <capability>:<HMAC-SHA256(nonce, capability)>' where capability ∈ {supervision, scripting, input}. The helper derives the expected MAC per capability at startup from --token; constant-time compare as today (SupervisionServiceImpl pattern).
2. SCOPING: HelperClient.Connect gains a capability set; Bevel.Ipc exposes typed sub-clients (SupervisionClient, ScriptingClient, InputClient) each attaching only its own capability header. App composition decides which sub-clients a component receives — e.g. the AE dispatcher gets scripting but never input.
3. HELPER SIDE: each Swift service impl validates ONLY its own capability's MAC, so a leaked scripting MAC cannot call InputService. Unknown/missing capability → RPCError(.unauthenticated), same as today.

title: BevelHelper answers RPCs without peer-credential/nonce check (IPC-04)
description: The deleted main.swift documented that the helper 'verifies the peer credential + nonce (IPC-04)' before answering RPCs. The replacement (native/helper-macos/Sources/BevelHelper/*.swift) parses/requires --token but never passes it to the service, and Ping is answered unconditionally with no SO_PEERCRED/getpeereid peer-uid check. The UDS lives in a world-accessible temp dir (Path.GetTempPath()/bevel-helper, HelperLifecycle.cs:44), so any local process can call the helper. Fix: enforce the --token/nonce and check the peer uid before serving RPCs, restrict socket dir perms.

Peer-UID transport check deferred to bevel-kyf (blocked on grpc-swift-2 handler API; redundant with 0700 dir + nonce for the cross-user threat).

title: FileOperationService._cts shared field: dispose/cross-cancel race
description: FileOperationService.cs:63-64 assigns the per-call 'using' linked CTS to the shared field _cts; Cancel() (:81) and in-job _cts?.Cancel() (:223,:376) read it with no synchronization. After ExecuteAsync returns the linked CTS is disposed but _cts still points to it -> a later UI Cancel() throws ObjectDisposedException. Two overlapping ExecuteAsync calls clobber _cts so operation A's internal cancel actually cancels operation B. Fix: pass the CTS through the call graph instead of a shared field, or track per-operation state and null/guard _cts on completion.

title: LocalDirectoryWatcher.Notify races Dispose -> ObjectDisposedException on threadpool

A queued FSW event delivered after disposal calls OnNext on a disposed Subject -> ObjectDisposedException on a background thread (no catch) during rapid folder navigation (FileManagerWindow.LoadDirectory disposes the old watcher on each navigate). Fix: guard OnNext against disposal (dispose flag + lock, or check _subject.IsDisposed) and swallow post-dispose notifications.

close_reason: Fixed with unit tests: VfsPath canonical parse/combine (VfsPathTests), enumerate TOCTOU guard + watcher dispose race + type-desc dedup (LocalFsProviderResilienceTests). Core 57/57 green.

title: HelperClient gRPC 'unix://' channel has no ConnectCallback -> never connects
description: src/Bevel.Ipc/HelperClient.cs:25-31 builds GrpcChannel.ForAddress('unix://<path>') with only Insecure credentials and no SocketsHttpHandler.ConnectCallback opening a UnixDomainSocketEndPoint. Grpc.Net.Client cannot dial a UDS without that callback, so PingAsync never connects and HelperLifecycle.WaitForReadyAsync (:109) times out after 5s. Currently masked because the host is never started (see bevel-c0y), but this blocks the helper the moment that is fixed. Fix: set GrpcChannelOptions.HttpHandler = new SocketsHttpHandler { ConnectCallback = ... UnixDomainSocketEndPoint(socketPath) } and use http://localhost as the address.
acceptance_criteria: HelperClient.PingAsync connects to the helper over the Unix domain socket.
close_reason: Fixed + tested. HelperLifecycle: single self-healing monitor loop started once in StartAsync (never spawns duplicates on restart), non-blocking graceful start (missing/broken helper no longer aborts boot — enables host start), backoff on repeated failures (mox). HelperClient: SocketsHttpHandler.ConnectCallback dials the Unix domain socket via UnixDomainSocketEndPoint (cwv). New Bevel.Pal.MacOS.Tests: HelperLifecycleTests (3) + HelperClientTests (4), 7/7 green.

title: SearchPaneViewModel.StopSearch disposes CTS still in use by the walk
description: SearchPaneViewModel.cs:104-110: WalkAsync is fire-and-forget (:100) and keeps enumerating with _searchCts.Token, but StopSearch calls Cancel() then Dispose() then null. Disposing a CTS whose token is still registered inside 'await foreach' throws ObjectDisposedException (not OperationCanceledException), escaping the catch(OperationCanceledException) filters and becoming an unobserved task exception. Triggered on every Stop / new-search-while-running. Fix: don't Dispose the CTS until the walk task has completed (await it, or dispose in a continuation), or swap-then-dispose the old CTS after the task ends.
acceptance_criteria: Cancelling or restarting a search never throws ObjectDisposedException.
close_reason: Fixed + tested. SearchPaneViewModel: walk owns CTS lifetime (disposed only after the walk, never mid-use) + guarded Stop/Dispose (u0z); content search reads via provider OpenReadAsync for all schemes (5ya). ItemView.SortAsync: shared ApplyOrder detaches ItemsSource and never drops streamed late arrivals (rn9). New SearchPaneViewModelTests (4) + ItemViewSortTests (4). FileManager 28/28.

title: LocalFsProvider enumerate: uncaught GetAttributes TOCTOU aborts whole listing
description: LocalFsProvider.cs:45 calls File.GetAttributes(entry) inside the EnumerateFileSystemEntries loop with no try/catch. If another process deletes/moves the entry between enumeration and GetAttributes, it throws FileNotFoundException/IOException and the whole IAsyncEnumerable terminates -> pane shows partial/zero items instead of skipping the vanished entry. Reproducible in busy folders (Downloads, build/temp). Fix: wrap the per-entry stat in try/catch and 'continue' on transient IO/not-found.
acceptance_criteria: Enumerating a folder while entries vanish yields the surviving entries without aborting.
close_reason: Fixed with unit tests: VfsPath canonical parse/combine (VfsPathTests), enumerate TOCTOU guard + watcher dispose race + type-desc dedup (LocalFsProviderResilienceTests). Core 57/57 green.

title: HelperLifecycle restart spawns duplicate monitor loops
description: HelperLifecycle.cs: on exit detection MonitorLoopAsync (:167) calls LaunchAndConnectAsync, which unconditionally assigns a NEW _monitorCts and a NEW _monitorTask=MonitorLoopAsync(...) (:101-102). The current loop keeps running under its old, now-unreferenced token (never cancelled). After N crashes there are N+1 concurrent monitor loops; the next crash makes all of them KillHelper()+relaunch simultaneously -> duplicate helper processes, orphaned CTSs, NRE races on _helperProcess. StopAsync only cancels the latest CTS. Fix: restart in-place within the existing loop (don't recurse into LaunchAndConnectAsync's monitor-spawn), or cancel/await the prior loop before starting a new one.
acceptance_criteria: Repeated helper crashes leave exactly one monitor loop and one helper process.
close_reason: Fixed + tested. HelperLifecycle: single self-healing monitor loop started once in StartAsync (never spawns duplicates on restart), non-blocking graceful start (missing/broken helper no longer aborts boot — enables host start), backoff on repeated failures (mox). HelperClient: SocketsHttpHandler.ConnectCallback dials the Unix domain socket via UnixDomainSocketEndPoint (cwv). New Bevel.Pal.MacOS.Tests: HelperLifecycleTests (3) + HelperClientTests (4), 7/7 green.

title: ItemView.SortAsync drops items streamed during sort + virtualization crash
description: ItemView.axaml.cs:242-266: for lists >=500, SortAsync snapshots _viewModels, awaits an off-thread sort, then _viewModels.Clear() + re-adds ONLY the stale snapshot. Rows appended by streaming AddItems during the await are silently lost (large dirs are exactly the ones still streaming). Also, unlike SortItems (:280 nulls ItemsPresenter.ItemsSource first 'to avoid virtualization teardown crash'), SortAsync mutates the still-bound collection, risking that crash. Fix: detach ItemsSource before mutating; re-apply the sort to the live collection (or merge post-sort additions) instead of replacing with a stale snapshot.
acceptance_criteria: Sorting a large directory mid-stream keeps all items and does not crash.
close_reason: Fixed + tested. title: SettingsService: shared SQLite _connection used by ReloadIfChangedAsync without _writeLock
description: Surfaced (not introduced) during bevel-ha3x review: the single shared _connection is used by the write path under _writeLock and by the 750ms ReloadIfChangedAsync poll WITHOUT the lock. Microsoft.Data.Sqlite doesn't support concurrent commands on one connection; if the poll fires during a write's async window a collision is possible. Pre-existing (the old SaveAsync+file-write await had the same exposure); the CAS retry loop slightly lengthens the window. Fix: gate ReloadIfChangedAsync's read under _writeLock too, or give the poller its own read connection.
close_reason: Dissolved by bevel-6nve: peers no longer open settings.db at all (RemoteSettingsService is push-based over IPC), so the poller-vs-writer shared-connection race no longer exists. The core's single SettingsService still uses _writeLock, and with core the sole writer there is no concurrent-command contention.

title: SettingsService: optimistic-concurrency (CAS) write to stop concurrent edits clobbering
description: ce-code-review session E, adversarial P2 (advisory) — SPLIT OUT of bevel-lha4 (whose other four items are done). SettingsService is last-writer-wins over one JSON blob: SerializeRaw writes ALL of _settings, so if two surfaces (e.g. the Settings window + an Explorer window) save DIFFERENT keys between one process's Load and Save, one side's change is silently clobbered. Fix: make WriteRowAsync a compare-and-swap — UPDATE settings SET json=$json, version=version+1 WHERE id=1 AND version=$expected (pass the last-loaded _version); on 0 rows affected, reload the peer's blob, RE-APPLY this process's pending delta on top, and retry (bounded, then last-writer-wins fallback). Requires UpdateAsync to own the retry loop (it holds the Action<BevelSettings> delta to re-apply). CAUTION: load-bearing persistence path with migration/pruning subtleties (SerializeRaw/MigrateRaw/ApplyRaw) — needs careful testing incl. a two-instance concurrent-different-keys test. Deliberately deferred from the audit's mechanical pass as higher-risk for only advisory severity.
close_reason: Delta write paths (UpdateAsync/UpdateThemeOverridesAsync) now CAS-merge: bounded retry over 'UPDATE ... version=version+1 WHERE version=$expected RETURNING version'; on miss, reload+migrate+re-apply delta so different-key edits merge; LWW fallback on exhaustion; whole-blob SaveAsync (tests-only) stays LWW. Existing version column reused, no DDL. Subteam, both verifiers SOUND (confirmed new tests fail under LWW, pass under CAS). 796 green.
